newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GRAIN PRICES SEEN JUST UP UNTIL END Q2- ARR.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GRAIN PRICES SEEN JUST UP UNTIL END Q2- ARR.

text.p: Polish wheat and rye prices are expected to inch up slightly until the end of the second quarter of the year, a monthly bulletin published by the government's Farm Market Agency (ARR) showed on Wednesday.
The bulletin, dated April, said that in June wheat prices should form around 53-55 zlotys per quintal while rye prices were likely to be around 41-43 zlotys per quintal.
Poland's Central Statistical Office (GUS) said that the wheat procurement price was 52.84 zlotys per quintal in March, while rye was at 40.73 zloyts.
The ARR said that stable grain prices over the last year would likely keep wheat and rye prices from seasonally falling around this year's harvest, due in August and September.
It said that farmers should sell wheat from this year's harvest at around 51-54 zlotys per quintal and rye at around 39-41 zlotys per quintal.
The bulletin said that year's grain output was difficult to judge after heavy winter losses, but that the ARR expected this year's harvest relatively flat from 1996's 24.7 million tonnes.
